transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Ever since that robbery, I keep organizing my whole life around avoiding anything that reminds me of it—certain neighborhoods, late meetings, even some community events. It's gotten to the point where I feel like I'm arranging my entire schedule just to avoid feeling unsafe.
To help me understand your situation better, how long ago did this robbery happen, and how long have you been experiencing these feelings and avoidance behaviors?

The robbery itself happened a little under two years ago. These feelings and the avoidance started creeping in a few months after that, and they've been hanging over me steadily for well over a year now.
Do you also experience unwanted, distressing memories, nightmares, or sudden flashbacks of the robbery?

Yes, if I hear a loud male voice or lock up an office, I’ll suddenly feel like I'm back on that floor with the gun at my head and my chest gets incredibly tight. At night, my mind just replays the whole thing, and I constantly wake up with my heart racing.
Since the robbery, do you find yourself constantly on guard, unusually jumpy, or easily startled by sudden noises?

Yes, I am constantly on guard now, always checking exits and watching who is coming and going whenever I'm out. I also jump out of my skin if someone walks up behind me at work or a car door slams, leaving my heart racing and my whole body tense for several minutes. It feels like I can never truly relax because my body is always on high alert.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, how you view yourself or the world, or your ability to feel positive emotions since the robbery?

I constantly blame myself for being at the store so late, and I've come to view the world as a dangerous, ugly place where I can never let my guard down. Even things that used to bring me joy, like my salsa classes or taking my granddaughter to the museum, now feel completely flat, as if I'm just going through the motions.

latest_inference.note: The patient presents with classic symptoms of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) following a traumatic event (a robbery with a gun to their head) about two years ago. The symptoms include persistent re-experiencing (flashbacks, nightmares, physiological reactivity), active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, hyperarousal (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response), and negative alterations in mood and cognition (self-blame, negative world view, anhedonia). These symptoms have persisted for over a year, causing significant distress and impairment. All ICD-10 criteria for F43.1 are met, allowing for a confident final diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) under ICD-10/DSM-5. They experienced a qualifying traumatic event (an armed robbery with a gun to their head) nearly two years ago. Since then, they have exhibited persistent intrusion symptoms (flashbacks, nightmares, physiological reactivity), avoidance of trauma-related reminders, negative alterations in cognitions and mood (self-blame, negative worldview, anhedonia), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response). These symptoms have persisted for well over a year and cause significant functional impairment.
